error_examples.summary: An employer must have an emergency action plan.
error_examples.rationale: An employer operating in a general industry workplace where no OSHA standard in Part 1910 specifically mandates an emergency action plan would be required to maintain one under the draft's unconditional rule, whereas the source requires one only 'whenever an OSHA standard in this part requires one'. The draft drops this critical condition of applicability and also omits the sentence establishing that § 1910.38's requirements apply to each such plan. Consequently, scope and summary are erroneous.

error_examples.summary: When an OSHA standard in this part requires an emergency action plan, it must be in writing, kept in the workplace, and available to employees for review.
error_examples.rationale: An employer with 10 or fewer employees who chooses to communicate the emergency action plan orally would violate the draft's unqualified requirement that the plan must be in writing, kept in the workplace, and available for review, whereas the source explicitly exempts such employers by allowing oral communication. The draft correctly incorporates the governing applicability lead-in from § 1910.38(a) but fails to qualify the written mandate with the explicit small-employer exception, making the summary incomplete.
